nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of length at most $140$ over a linearly ordered type and let $k$ be a natural number. If median-of-medians selection of rank $k$ in $L$ returns an element $x$, then $x$ occurs in $L$, the number of entries of $L$ less than $x$, counted with multiplicity, is at most $k$, and $k$ is less than the number of entries of $L$ that are at most $x$.
nodes.title: Correctness of median-of-medians selection on short lists

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of length $n \le 140$ over a linearly ordered type and every natural number $k$, median-of-medians selection of rank $k$ in $L$ is charged at most $80n$ comparisons.
nodes.title: Comparison bound for median-of-medians selection on short lists

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $m$ and $p$ be natural numbers with $n \ge 140$, $m \le \lfloor (n + 4)/5 \rfloor$ and $p \le \lfloor 7n/10 \rfloor + 6$. Then $20m + 20p + n \le 20n$.
nodes.title: Size budget for the two median-of-medians recursive calls

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $m$, $p$, $a$, $c_1$ and $c_2$ be natural numbers with $n \ge 140$, $m \le \lfloor (n + 4)/5 \rfloor$, $p \le \lfloor 7n/10 \rfloor + 6$, $c_1 \le 20am$ and $c_2 \le 20ap$. Then $c_1 + c_2 + an \le 20an$.
nodes.title: Cost budget for one median-of-medians step

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list over a linearly ordered type and let $k$ be a natural number. If median-of-medians selection of rank $k$ in $L$ returns an element $x$, then $x$ occurs in $L$, the number of entries of $L$ less than $x$, counted with multiplicity, is at most $k$, and $k$ is less than the number of entries of $L$ that are at most $x$.
nodes.title: Correctness of median-of-medians selection

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ over a linearly ordered type and every natural number $k$, median-of-medians selection of rank $k$ in $L$ returns the entry at zero-based position $k$ of the insertion sort of $L$ by $\le$ when $k$ is less than the length of $L$, and returns nothing otherwise.
nodes.title: Median-of-medians selection agrees with sorting

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ over a linearly ordered type and every natural number $k$, median-of-medians selection of rank $k$ in $L$ returns nothing if and only if $k$ is at least the length of $L$.
nodes.title: Median-of-medians selection fails exactly on out-of-range ranks

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ over a linearly ordered type and every natural number $k$ at least the length of $L$, median-of-medians selection of rank $k$ in $L$ returns nothing and is charged zero comparisons.
nodes.title: Out-of-range ranks cost no comparisons

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of length at most $140$ over a linearly ordered type and every natural number $k$, median-of-medians selection of rank $k$ in $L$ coincides with timed quickselect of rank $k$ in $L$: both return the same result and are charged the same number of comparisons.
nodes.title: Median-of-medians selection is quickselect on short lists

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ over a linearly ordered type and every natural number $k$ less than the length of $L$, median-of-medians selection of rank $k$ in $L$ returns some element.
nodes.title: Median-of-medians selection succeeds on valid ranks

nodes.summary: Let $xs$ be a list over a linear order, and let $g_1, \dots, g_m$ be its consecutive blocks of five elements, the last of which may be shorter. Then the list of group medians of $xs$ has the same length $m$, say $x_1, \dots, x_m$, and for each $i$, writing $k_i = \lfloor (|g_i| - 1)/2 \rfloor$ and counting elements of $g_i$ with multiplicity: $x_i$ belongs to $g_i$, at most $k_i$ elements of $g_i$ are less than…
nodes.title: Group medians are lower medians of their blocks

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ of length $n$ over a linear order, the list of group medians of $xs$ has exactly $\lfloor (n + 4)/5 \rfloor = \lceil n/5 \rceil$ entries.
nodes.title: Number of group medians

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linear order, every entry of the list of group medians of $xs$ is an element of $xs$.
nodes.title: Group medians come from the input

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ of length $n$ over a linear order, computing the group medians of $xs$ takes at most $2n$ comparisons.
nodes.title: Comparison cost of the group medians

nodes.summary: Given a list $xs$ over a linear order, split $xs$ into consecutive blocks of five elements, the last of which may be shorter. Sort each block $g$ by insertion sort and return, in block order, the entry at position $\lfloor (|g| - 1)/2 \rfloor$ (counting from $0$) of each sorted block, that is, its lower median. The cost is the total number of comparisons made by these insertion sorts.
nodes.title: Group medians for median-of-medians selection

nodes.summary: Let $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $a \in \mathbb{N}$. Suppose that $T(n) \le 20an$ for every $n \le 140$, and that for every $n > 140$ there are $m, p \in \mathbb{N}$ with $m \le \lfloor (n + 4)/5 \rfloor$, $p \le \lfloor 7n/10 \rfloor + 6$ and $T(n) \le T(m) + T(p) + an$. Then $T(n) \le 20an$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Linear solution of the median-of-medians recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a nonempty list of length $n$ over a linear order, and let $k = \lfloor (n - 1)/2 \rfloor$. Then median-of-medians selection on $L$ at zero-based rank $k$ returns an element $x$ of $L$ such that at most $k$ entries of $L$ are less than $x$ and more than $k$ entries of $L$ are at most $x$, where entries are counted with repetition.
nodes.title: Median of medians finds the lower median

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list without repeated entries over a linear order and let $k \in \mathbb{N}$. If median-of-medians selection on $L$ at zero-based rank $k$ returns an element $x$, then the set $\{y \in L : y \le x\}$ has exactly $k + 1$ elements.
nodes.title: Set rank of a median-of-medians result

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list without repeated entries over a linear order, of length $n$, and let $1 \le i \le n$. Then median-of-medians selection on $L$ at zero-based rank $i - 1$ returns an element $x$ of $L$, and the set $\{y \in L : y \le x\}$ has exactly $i$ elements.
nodes.title: Median of medians selects every one-based rank

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list without repeated entries over a linear order and let $i \ge 1$. If median-of-medians selection on $L$ at zero-based rank $i - 1$ returns an element $x$, then the set $\{y \in L : y \le x\}$ has exactly $i$ elements.
nodes.title: One-based rank of a median-of-medians result

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of length $n$ over a linear order and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, median-of-medians selection on $L$ at rank $k$ charges at most $80n$ comparisons, where $n$ counts repeated entries.
nodes.title: Median of medians makes linearly many comparisons

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a nonempty list of length $n$ over a linear order, and let $k = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. Then median-of-medians selection on $L$ at zero-based rank $k$ returns an element $x$ of $L$ such that at most $k$ entries of $L$ are less than $x$ and more than $k$ entries of $L$ are at most $x$, where entries are counted with repetition.
nodes.title: Median of medians finds the upper median

nodes.summary: Given a list $L$ over a linear order and a zero-based rank $k$, median-of-medians selection returns either an element of $L$ or nothing, charging one unit of cost per order comparison. If $k \ge |L|$, where $|L|$ is the length of $L$, it returns nothing at no cost.
